title: Headroom negotiation and granular GPU budgeting for mixed weights/KV/activations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Serving runtime must allocate GPU memory across three orthogonal sinks (weights, KV cache, activations) while preserving headroom for bursts and continuous batching. Current heuristics either over-reserve (wasting capacity and increasing cost) or under-reserve (evictions, OOMs, and request throttling).
goals: Define a compact, testable memory budget model that expresses per-tenant allocation across weights/KV/activations and a dynamic headroom reserve
Implement a negotiation/placement algorithm the scheduler can use to make admission decisions for mixed workloads (small chat requests + long-context generation + embeddings)
Provide telemetry and simulators to validate budget policies under bursty, multimodal traffic patterns
Produce a rollout plan with canary guardrails and automatic fallback to safe-reserve policy
scope: Design the budget formula and policy knobs (static share vs percentile-based headroom)
Integrate budget checks into the admission path and continuous-batching planner
Add KV cache accounting per-tenant + tag eviction priority buckets
Build a fast simulator for mixed workloads to evaluate tail risk and median cost impact
Expose metrics in Console: per-tenant memory breakdown, headroom utilization, eviction events
acceptance_criteria: New budget API returns per-tenant budget breakdown and headroom recommendation
Admission path rejects/queues requests if projected usage + requested allocation exceeds available budget with headroom margin
Simulator shows <1% increase in tail OOMs for 95th%-based headroom on our standard mixed workload traces compared to current conservative policy
End-to-end integration test that reproduces a synthetic surge and verifies automatic fallback to safe-reserve without client-visible errors
Console shows new memory breakdown dashboard and corresponding alerts for headroom pressure
progress_updates: 2025-02-13: Kickoff meeting with runtime, scheduler, and telemetry. Agreed on initial memory model: weights (pinned), KV (cacheable), activations (ephemeral).
2025-02-18: Prototype budget formula implemented in simulator: base_alloc = model_weights + tenant_min_kv; headroom = max(percentile(usage, 95) * factor, absolute_min). Ran 1000 trace simulations.
2025-02-25: Found corner case: long-context generation + small embedding requests cause KV churn that invalidates percentile-based headroom. Added transient multiplier for KV write-heavy bursts.
2025-02-28: PR 7321 opened with admission check integration and lightweight metric emissions (headroom_requested, headroom_reserved).
2025-03-03: Internal perf run on staging with 8-GPU cluster: median cost reduced by ~7% for mixed traffic, but 99.9th latency spikes in one tenant—investigating eviction policy interaction.
experiments: Sim-001: baseline conservative reserve (20% of free) vs dynamic 95th-percentile headroom. Result: dynamic lowered steady-state cost 9% but increased eviction count by 12% under synthetic KV-flash bursts.
Sim-002: KV-priority buckets (hot pinned, warm LRU, cold eviction) reduced spike-induced evictions from 12% to 4% with similar cost savings.

Perf-001: Staging replay of production traffic for 24h with dynamic headroom + transient KV multiplier. Observed 1 OOM event across 3M requests; root cause traced to activation oversubscription for a model variant.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Dynamic headroom underestimates rare heavy-context requests -> mitigation: maintain absolute_min reserve and per-tenant max_alloc cap
Risk: KV accounting adds CPU overhead -> mitigation: sample-based accounting and periodic reconciliation rather than per-request ops
Risk: Metric signal delay causes misinformed admission decisions -> mitigation: conservative smoothing and short-timescale emergency reserve activation
decisions: Adopt hybrid headroom: primary percentile-based with an absolute floor and burst multiplier for KV-heavy patterns
Expose two knobs to customers: desired economization_level (aggressive|balanced|safe) and tenant_max_alloc
Integrate simulator as part of CI for any change to budget formula or eviction policy
next_steps: Complete PR reviews for runtime and scheduler merges (owners: @miguel, @zara)
Add end-to-end chaos test: inject KV-flash bursts and verify no client-visible errors for 99.99% of requests
Instrument additional histograms for headroom utilization and surface them in Console
Schedule canary rollout to 5% of traffic with automatic rollback if OOMs or latency SLO violations > threshold
